notes:
Account summary: Hawthorne EdgeWorks is a mid-size enterprise retail-tech platform (owns merchant personalization stack). Primary drivers: strict cost-by-tenant forecasting, direct control of model runtime, and data residency.

Why lost: After an extended POC Redwood ran well but procurement hit a budget freeze and the infra team recommended an in-house self-hosted stack (vLLM + TGI on NVidia TensorRT) to reduce per-token costs and keep all models behind their network boundary. CTO quote: "We need full control over caching, kernel selection and cost — can't accept another managed black box right now."

Security: Completed initial questionnaire; legal required on-prem KMS/HSM proof and long-term retention controls. Security team more comfortable with an internal TensorRT deployment they can audit.

Sales notes: Opportunity progressed through discovery -> POC -> security review -> procurement. POC highlights were strong latency and throughput on Dedicated config. Recommend keeping relationship warm: send a short migration checklist, offer private deployment starter docs, and schedule a 6-month check-in.

Short wins: Redwood performance benchmark report shareable; provided cost comparison vs self-host (customer said internal infra team found cheaper at scale with TensorRT + TGI).

Customer sentiment: pragmatic, cost-driven, conservative on third-party managed infra. No current CSM engagement (deal closed-lost).
